title: With `autoflush=False`, queries do not see rows that were just added.
comment:
**With `autoflush=False`, queries do not see rows that were just added.**

The services often call `db.add(...)` and then query the same table before they flush:
- `handle_link_down` (`backend/app/services/switch.py` Lines 132-176) adds new `TaskLinkBinding` rows and then runs `calc_occupancy`/`recalc_all`. The new bindings are not visible, so the target link load stays stale. The overload warning and the plan generation are missed.
- `_dispatch_parsed` demand_change (`backend/app/services/engine.py` Lines 555-556) runs `recalc_all` before the new demand is flushed.
- In the `recalc_all` imminent path (`backend/app/services/occupancy.py` Lines 326-338), the old plans are set to `已作废` but not flushed. The SQL `WHERE status='待审批'` in `generate_plans` still returns them, so the function returns early and generates no new plans.

Remove `autoflush=False`. The SQLAlchemy default is `True`.
<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
 SessionLocal = sessionmaker(
     bind=engine,
-    autoflush=False,
     autocommit=False,
```
</details>

title: The restore notice always fails after a real outage.
comment:
**The restore notice always fails after a real outage.**

`handle_link_down` sets the faulted link to `down`. In the input flow, nothing sets it back to `up`. The `actual_finish_min` path in `handle_repair_update` is never called. "线路1已恢复" therefore always raises `链路未处于 up 状态`, and the task never moves back. The restore notice is the signal that the link is up again. Set `link.oper_state = "up"` and write a `state_changed` event here instead of rejecting the request.

title: The preset fault booking never fires.
comment:
**The preset fault booking never fires.**

`EVT-0001` stores `ref_code='AL-01'`. `_dispatch_booking` treats `ref_code` as a link code and calls `db.get(CommLink, "AL-01")`. That returns `None`, so the function returns without action. The event is still marked as fulfilled, so the T+15 L-1H fault never happens. Seed `ref_code` with `'L-1H'`.
<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-('EVT-0001','task_booked','alarm','AL-01',15,'15分钟后线路1故障，预订为T+15兑现'),
+('EVT-0001','task_booked','alarm','L-1H',15,'15分钟后线路1故障，预订为T+15兑现'),
```
</details>

title: `/scene/decide` cannot approve a pending plan.
comment:
**`/scene/decide` cannot approve a pending plan.**

`ApprovalRecord` rows are created only inside `_do_decide`, after a decision. For a plan that is still pending, `db.get(ApprovalRecord, ...)` always returns `None`, so the route always returns 404. If a record does exist, the plan is already decided, and `_do_decide` raises because the status is not `待审批`. Accept `plan_code`, as the OpenAPI spec says, and call `decide` directly.

title: Binding folding does not check that the task's latest binding is on this link.
comment:
**Binding folding does not check that the task's latest binding is on this link.**

- `_current_load_on_link` counts every task that was ever bound to the link, including tasks that have moved away. The capacity is overcounted and candidates can be skipped by mistake.
- The release check sets `any_task = True` on the first row. A holder link that had any binding is therefore never released, and `released_links` is always empty.

Compare each task's global latest binding with the link, as `_candidates` does, before you count the task or mark the link as busy.





Also applies to: 185-196

title: `extractlink` breaks link codes that already contain a hyphen.
comment:
**`_extract_link` breaks link codes that already contain a hyphen.**

For an input such as `l-1h`, `upper()` gives `L-1H`. `.replace("L", "L-")` then gives `L--1H`, which is not in the allowed set. The case-sensitive keyword fallback also fails for lowercase input, so the function returns `None`. Normalize the code from the digit instead.
<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    m = re.search(r"L-?\dH", text, re.IGNORECASE)
+    m = re.search(r"L-?(\d)H", text, re.IGNORECASE)
     if m:
-        s = m.group(0).upper().replace("L", "L-").replace("L-", "L-")
-        if not s.startswith("L-"):
-            s = "L-" + s[1:]
+        s = f"L-{m.group(1)}H"
         if s in ("L-1H", "L-2H", "L-3H"):
             return s
```
</details>

title: `resetscene` does not make the scenario replayable.
comment:
**`reset_scene` does not make the scenario replayable.**

`_tick_once` changes fulfilled bookings to `event_type="state_changed"` (Lines 74-75). `reset_scene` only clears the clock and `_CONSUMED_EVENTS`. After one run, the preset bookings, link states, alarms, plans and bindings stay mutated, and the next start replays nothing. The OpenAPI `/scene/reset` summary promises a restore of the default data. Reset the business tables to the seed state, or at least restore the `task_booked` events.

title: The tick loop never starts, and WebSocket pushes from sync routes are dropped.
comment:
**The tick loop never starts, and WebSocket pushes from sync routes are dropped.**

`/scene/start` and `/scene/resume` are plain `def` routes. FastAPI runs them in a threadpool, so `asyncio.get_running_loop()` raises `RuntimeError` and `_LOOP_TASK` stays `None`. Booked events are never fulfilled and `state` is never pushed. The same pattern silently drops every `loop.create_task(_push())` in `occupancy.py`, `plan.py`, `switch.py`, `restore.py` and `repair.py` when they run from sync routes. Start `_engine_loop` in a FastAPI lifespan or startup hook. Make the control routes `async def`, or send pushes through a captured main loop with `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`.

title: `generateplansforalarm` ignores its `alarmcode` argument.
comment:
**`generate_plans_for_alarm` ignores its `alarm_code` argument.**

The function passes only `alarm.link_code`. `generate_plans` then picks the latest `容量超限` alarm on that link, and it falls back to any alarm only if none exists. When `_dispatch_booking` or `_dispatch_parsed` creates a `link_down` alarm on a link that has an older capacity alarm, the plans are attached to the old alarm. They can also return early because the old alarm's plans are still pending. Pass `alarm_code` into `generate_plans` and use it directly.

title: The primary key `(taskcode, assignedmin)` collides when a task is rebound twice in the same minute.
comment:
**The primary key `(task_code, assigned_min)` collides when a task is rebound twice in the same minute.**

`now_min()` returns `0` until the scene starts and stays `0` for the first 60 s after it starts. The seed bindings use `assigned_min=0`. A switch, reroute or restore at minute 0 therefore inserts a duplicate key such as `(T-A, 0)`, and the flush fails with an IntegrityError. A switch followed by a reroute approval in the same scene minute fails the same way. Ordering by `assigned_min` also makes ties ambiguous. Add a surrogate auto-increment PK, or a monotonic sequence column, and order by that column. Change `通信任务保障建表与初始化脚本.sql` Line 95 to match.

title: Use one WebSocket message envelope.
comment:
**Use one WebSocket message envelope.**

`broadcast` sends `{"type", "payload"}`. The initial push in `backend/app/api/scene.py` (Line 97) sends `{"type", "data"}`, and the OpenAPI `/scene/ws` description documents `data`. A client that reads `data` gets `undefined` for every broadcast message. Use `data` everywhere, or update both the spec and the initial push to use `payload`.

title: `estfinishmin` is a relative duration, but this check treats it as an absolute minute.
comment:
**`est_finish_min` is a relative duration, but this check treats it as an absolute minute.**

The parser extracts "预计55分钟完成" as `55`, which is a duration. `request_repair` also stores `link.avg_repair_min` (a duration), and `generate_plans` uses `now + avg_repair_min`. This check compares the raw value to `dead_line`. For example, at `now=40` with "预计20分钟", the repair finishes at minute 60, which is after the deadline of 50. The plan is still marked `能赶上`. Compare `now + est_finish_min` instead, and store the absolute value if that is what the column means.

title: The auto-timeout path deadlocks on `DECIDELOCK`.
comment:
**The auto-timeout path deadlocks on `_DECIDE_LOCK`.**

`_runner` acquires `_DECIDE_LOCK` and then calls `decide()`, which runs `async with _DECIDE_LOCK` again. `asyncio.Lock` is not reentrant, so the task waits forever. After that, every later human `decide()` also blocks on the lock. A second problem exists: `_do_decide` calls `_cancel_countdown_async(alarm_code)`, which pops and cancels the current task. That would abort the automatic decision. Call `_do_decide` directly under the lock. Remove the task's own entry from `_COUNTDOWN_TASKS` before the decision instead of cancelling itself.
<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-            async with _DECIDE_LOCK:
-                await decide(
+            async with _COUNTDOWN_LOCK:
+                if _COUNTDOWN_TASKS.get(alarm_code) is asyncio.current_task():
+                    _COUNTDOWN_TASKS.pop(alarm_code, None)
+            async with _DECIDE_LOCK:
+                await _do_decide(
                     s,
-                    plan_code=default_plan.plan_code,
-                    decision="批准",
-                    reason="60 秒未决策，自动执行保守默认方案",
-                    approver="SYSTEM",
-                    decision_source="超时自动",
+                    default_plan.plan_code,
+                    "批准",
+                    "60 秒未决策，自动执行保守默认方案",
+                    "SYSTEM",
+                    "超时自动",
                 )
                 s.commit()
```
</details>

title: `decidesync` blocks the main event loop and runs `dodecide` on a second loop.
comment:
**`decide_sync` blocks the main event loop and runs `_do_decide` on a second loop.**

`/comm/approvals/decide` is `async def`, so this branch always runs. `future.result()` blocks the uvicorn event loop until the worker thread finishes. No other request or WebSocket is served during that time. In the worker thread, `asyncio.run` creates a new loop:
- `get_hub().broadcast` awaits WebSocket sends that belong to the main loop. These sends fail, and `broadcast` then removes every client from the hub.
- `_cancel_countdown_async` calls `task.cancel()` on a main-loop task from another thread, which is not thread-safe.

Make the route call `await decide(...)` directly, and remove the thread/`asyncio.run` bridge.

title: The OpenAPI contract does not match the implemented routes.
comment:
**The OpenAPI contract does not match the implemented routes.**

This spec documents `/comm/switch`, `/comm/occupancy`, `/comm/plan`, `/comm/approve`, `/comm/repair`, `/comm/alarm`, `/comm/restore`, `/comm/task`, `/comm/link`, `/comm/demand` and `/comm/snapshot`. `backend/app/api/comm.py` does not implement any of these paths. It implements `/comm/alarms/inject`, `/comm/switch/{link_code}`, `/comm/plans/generate/{alarm_code}`, `/comm/approvals/decide`, `/comm/repairs/*`, `/comm/links/{link_code}/restore` and `/comm/input`. Other parts of the spec also do not match the code:
- `/scene/decide` documents `Sk04ApproveIn` with `plan_code`. `SceneDecideIn` requires `approval_code`.
- `/scene/start` documents `offset_min`. `start` in `backend/app/api/scene.py` ignores it.
- `/scene/reset` says it restores the default data. `reset_scene` only resets the clock.
- `SceneStateData.pending_approvals` is documented as `ApprovalItem[]`. `get_state` returns plan dicts.

A frontend built against this spec, or against the Apifox mock, gets 404s or wrong shapes when it calls the real backend. Make the spec and the routers agree before release.
